findings.body:
The early return `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` was removed. For an empty slice, `total` is 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so the integer division `total / 0` executes and Rust panics with divide-by-zero. The doc comment on line 1 still promises 0 for empty input.

Trigger: Calling `average(&[])` or any empty `&[u32]`.

Impact: Any caller of the public `average` function that passes an empty slice panics instead of receiving the documented 0. Within this repository, the only hit for `average(` is its definition, so no internal caller was found. External callers are unknown, so the crash depends on them passing empty input.
findings.suggestion: Restore the early return: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
findings.title: average() panics with divide-by-zero on empty input

risk_level.reason: The change removes the empty-slice guard, so average(&[]) now divides by zero and panics, and the sum can also overflow u32 without a check.

summary: Review complete: 1 finding(s) across 1 investigated file(s).
